links.note: Hypothesis test, not a result. Pre-data evidence is the freeze timestamp in this file and the S3 checkpoint pushed by the repository run gate; no local commit precedes the data (see PREREG.md section 4).

question: On the volcano census V2 curves (p = 42310123, r = 1322303, cofactor h = 32), does building the IC factor base from cofactor-projected points ([h]P, prime-projected-abscissa) instead of raw points (prime-abscissa), at the same 64 columns, the same mitm negation-folded oracle and the same targets, lower the end-to-end counted S, and by how much against the matched rho?

claims.text: With every unpriced native operation priced at w in {0, 0.1, 1} GAE on both arms, the paired end-to-end S gain G_w = mean S(ic-raw) / mean S(ic-clear) over the 112 V2 units has a 95% paired-bootstrap lower limit above 1 at every w.
claims.if_supported: cofactor clearing is a measured constant-factor improvement of the census ic baseline on this family (counted S, L1 host, same-host replay only)
claims.if_not_supported: the clear arm is not shown to beat the raw arm at the stated size; report the interval

claims.text: The point estimate of G_0 is at least 3 (the relayed Python estimate of 2.7x to 7.7x across volcanoes, reviewers 6.0x on V2, is falsified if the point estimate is below 3).

The positive control holds: rho-plain / rho-neg has a 95% lower limit above 1.2 (negation fold, about sqrt 2). The A/A ratio interval containing 1 and the companion h = 1 negative control (G_0 interval inside [0.95, 1.05]) are further preconditions, read from the control comparisons, not decisive comparisons.

hypotheses.statement: Projecting the factor base by the cofactor makes every pair-table entry a sum a subgroup target can hit, so trials per relation fall by about h and end-to-end S falls.
hypotheses.mechanism: [h] kills E[h] and is an automorphism of the prime-order subgroup; raw base points lie in cosets of E[h], so only a fraction of folded pair-table entries can match a subgroup target (LEAD-19).

predictions.minimum_effect: G_0 point estimate >= 3 and 95% lower limit > 1

positive.expected_detection: rho-plain / rho-neg priced S ratio with a 95% lower limit above 1.2 (negation fold, about sqrt 2)

negative.not_applicable_reason: ecbench compares whole sessions and cannot filter by population, so the h = 1 negative control runs as its own session under the companion protocol protocol-h1-control.json (same arms, same analysis script). It is a precondition of the verdict: if its G_0 95% interval is not inside [0.95, 1.05], the verdict here is invalid_controls.

power.note: no power calculation was run; this is an assumption. The interval is reported whatever its width. The 3x threshold is large relative to the interval width expected from 112 paired units (assumed relative half-width of order 10%). Correction: intersection-union over the three weights, no alpha adjustment.

preflight_runtime.measured_on: not measured on this spec: estimated from the 72-execution smoke run of the same binary on this host (5.9 s wall, 20-bit curve), scaled up; no pilot of this spec was run because it would show counted results

primary.name: end-to-end S gain, unpriced work at 0 GAE
primary.unit: ratio of totals sum S(ic-raw) / sum S(ic-clear)
primary.definition: over matched (workload, round) pairs of the 112 V2 workloads and 4 measured rounds, total S of ic-raw divided by total S of ic-clear; S is total GAE over the session floor, all phases (factor base, oracle set-up, relations, linear algebra, solve)
primary.source: records.jsonl cost.s; ecbench compare --a ic-clear --b ic-raw --weight 0

secondary.name: S gain at 0.1 GAE per unpriced native operation
secondary.definition: as M-gain-w0 with every unpriced native operation priced at 0.1 GAE on both arms

secondary.name: S gain at 1 GAE per unpriced native operation
secondary.definition: as M-gain-w0 at 1 GAE per unpriced native operation

secondary.name: trials per relation ratio (mechanism)
secondary.definition: phases[relations].native.trials / native.relations for ic-raw divided by the same for ic-clear; reported only

secondary.name: distance remaining to matched rho
secondary.unit: ratio of totals S(ic arm) / S(rho-neg)
secondary.definition: for ic-raw and ic-clear at each pricing weight; reported, not a gate
secondary.formula: sum S(ic arm) / sum S(rho-neg) over matched pairs

measurement.timed_primary_justification: the primary metric is counted S (group operations), valid at any isolation level; no wall-clock figure is a decision input

stopping_rules.rule: run all 2800 planned executions (112 units x 5 arms x 5 rounds including warm-up)
invalidate and report if any record is not verified, or the A/A, positive or negative control fails

decision_rule.text: supported if the 95% lower limit of G_w is above 1 at w = 0, 0.1 and 1; the 3x claim (C2) is falsified if the point estimate of G_0 is below 3 (the upper limit is reported separately); the result is void if any of the three controls fails. Multiplicity: the pass line is an intersection-union over the three pricing weights (every weight must pass at its own 95% interval), so no alpha adjustment is applied.
decision_rule.threshold: G_0 point estimate >= 3; lower limit of ci95 > 1 at each weight
decision_rule.statistic: ratio of totals B/A over matched (workload, round) pairs as defined in src/cryptanalysis/ecbench/compare.rs, workloads as clusters
decision_rule.interval: ecbench compare primary ci95 (linearised delta-method interval, workloads as clusters, Student t); the percentile bootstrap beside it (4000 resamples, seed 20261002) is reported too
